skill.name: grill-with-docs
skill.description: Challenges a software plan against the repository domain language, code, CONTEXT.md, and ADRs. It asks focused questions and updates living documentation when decisions settle.
skill.summary: Review design plans against project language, code, and architecture records.

content.value_statement: Design plans often drift from a project language and recorded decisions. This skill challenges assumptions, resolves terminology, and updates CONTEXT.md or ADRs as decisions settle.
actual_capabilities: Interviews the user one question at a time during design planning.
Reads existing CONTEXT.md, CONTEXT-MAP.md, and ADR files when present.
Checks user statements against repository code when the answer is discoverable.
Calls out conflicting or vague domain terms during the session.
Updates CONTEXT.md when terminology is resolved.
Suggests ADRs only for hard-to-reverse and surprising trade-off decisions.
limitations: Works best when the repository already contains useful code or documentation.
Requires user confirmation for ambiguous product or domain decisions.
Focuses on terminology and architecture documentation, not full implementation planning.
May need manual review for sensitive or regulated project decisions.

use_cases.title: Clarify a Feature Plan
use_cases.description: Challenge a proposed feature against the existing domain language before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Domain Terms
use_cases.description: Resolve overloaded terms and record a clear shared vocabulary in CONTEXT.md.

use_cases.title: Capture Architecture Decisions
use_cases.description: Decide whether a design trade-off deserves an ADR and draft it only when it adds value.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small design idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Challenge this plan against the project language and docs. Ask one question at a time and recommend an answer for each question.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Domain Terms
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate terminology cleanup before building a feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these terms for ambiguity. Compare them with CONTEXT.md and propose canonical names where the language conflicts.

prompt_templates.title: Check Code Against Claims
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced validation of a design assumption.
prompt_templates.prompt: I think the system behaves this way. Check the code and existing docs, then challenge any contradictions before we decide.

prompt_templates.title: Guide an ADR Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Help decide whether this trade-off needs an ADR. Verify that it is hard to reverse, surprising, and based on real alternatives.

output_examples.input: I want to add partial order cancellation to our checkout flow.
output_examples.output: The skill asks whether cancellation applies to an entire order or selected order lines, then checks the existing glossary and code before updating CONTEXT.md.

output_examples.input: We may replace synchronous billing calls with domain events.
output_examples.output: The skill tests the trade-off, asks about failure modes and ownership boundaries, then recommends whether the decision deserves an ADR.

output_examples.input: Our team uses account, customer, and user interchangeably.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the ambiguity, recommends canonical terms, and records avoided aliases after the user confirms the distinction.

best_practices: Start with a concrete plan or domain question, not a broad request for feedback.
Let the skill inspect existing CONTEXT.md and ADR files before naming new concepts.
Confirm each terminology decision before allowing documentation updates.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to create ADRs for reversible or routine implementation choices.
Accepting new domain terms without checking existing language first.
Batching many unresolved decisions into one prompt without answering the earlier questions.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It challenges software plans against project language, code behavior, CONTEXT.md, and architecture decision records.

faq.question: Does it write code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on planning, terminology, CONTEXT.md updates, and ADR creation when appropriate.

faq.question: Can it create new documentation files?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill creates CONTEXT.md or docs/adr files lazily when a confirmed decision needs to be recorded.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before implementing a meaningful feature, changing domain language, or making a durable architecture choice.

faq.question: How does it handle multiple contexts?
faq.answer: It uses CONTEXT-MAP.md when present, then asks when the relevant context is unclear.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
